item.title: Time Zones in Arizona, United States - timeanddate.com
item.description: Most of Arizona observes Mountain Standard Time (MST) all year. However, because the Navajo Nation observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), the corresponding DST designation, Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) is also listed here.

item.title: Arizona (AZ) time zone - WhichTimezone
item.description: All counties and cities of the state have the same time zone. Arizona does not observe daylight savings with the exception of the Navajo Nation Reservation in the north east, also referred to as “daylight savings donut”.

item.title: Time in Arizona - Wikipedia
item.description: Most of Arizona is in the Mountain Time Zone and observes Mountain Time. [2] Since 1968, most of the state—except the Navajo Nation —does not observe daylight saving time and remains on Mountain Standard Time (MST) all year.

item.title: Arizona Timezones Explained: It’s a Prickly Situation
item.description: In this article, I’ll break down what time zone Arizona is in and make sure that when you visit you’re not just a tourist, but a true Arizonan time wizard! So grab some cactus juice and let’s get started!

item.title: Current Time in Arizona (AZ) — Live Clock, Time Zone & DST
item.description: Arizona uses Mountain Standard Time (UTC-7). The state does not observe daylight saving time and stays on standard time year-round.

item.title: Time in Arizona, United States now
item.description: The time in Arizona is 2 hours behind the time in New York when New York is on standard time, and 3 hours behind the time in New York when New York is on daylight saving time. Arizona has not had daylight saving time since 1967. The IANA time zone identifier for Arizona is America/Phoenix.
